doc: Check, sample, point into, vary and render hanim animation documents (<name>.animation.omui.json) headless.

tools.name: document.check
tools.description: The document's plan (duration, tracks, segments, markers, stage size) and the operations it took, or every problem at its JSON pointer (syntax at line and column)

file.description: a file or directory path: a <name>.animation.omui.json

tools.name: document.sample
tools.description: Every object at given moments: drawn or not, position, scale, rotation, fill, group opacity and the bounds it covers

at.description: the moments in seconds, one --at each

tools.name: document.at
tools.description: What governs a moment someone points at: the steps that run then (of one object, if given), innermost first — each one's JSON pointer, start, end, how far through it is, the objects it moves and its own JSON: what to change to change what is seen

object.description: only the steps that move this object

tools.name: document.vary
tools.description: Alternatives a person picks from by looking: one value (at a JSON pointer) set several ways, every variant drawn at the same moments, a row each under the document as written — a sheet, each variant's document, and a report with each one's duration, frame hashes or problems

set.description: the JSON pointer of the value to vary (a key the step lacks is added)

value.description: each value, as JSON, one --value each (15 at most)

out.description: a file or directory path: the prefix of the files written

frames.description: evenly spaced over the longest variant (8 by default)

tools.name: document.render
tools.description: The stage drawn at evenly spaced or given moments: PNG frames (and SVG), a strip of them, an optional animated WebP and a report with each frame's pixel hash and objects

out.description: a file or directory path: the prefix of the files written

webp.description: frames a second of an animated WebP

svg.description: each frame as SVG too (vectors at any size; what SVG cannot say kept as pixels, counted per frame)
